Hannah / Marissa — looping in status update and initial artifacts.

Attached is a redacted sample of the erasure log for tenant id tenant123. It includes the deletion request id, initiating user/service, deletion timestamp, and verification checksum that our backend emits after garbage-collection completes. We have redacted user identifiers per the tracker guidance; full auditor copies can be produced under NDA if needed.

How the deletion pipeline works (short):
- Deletion request accepted via control-plane API or console -> request ID generated.
- Request validated against tenant ownership and retention exceptions.
- Async job enqueues a deletion operation across storage and KV caches.
- GC job runs, emits a post-delete verification record and stores a signed hash in the audit store.
- Our retention attestation job samples these records nightly and surfaces failures to PagerDuty.

I've uploaded a runbook excerpt and the full (redacted) log to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-banksecure-evidence.

Hannah / team — attaching the TTL enforcement snapshot and a short note on where TTLs are configured.

- TTLs are defined in our retention matrix (config repo) and compiled into runtime policies by the retention compiler.
- Enforcements live on the metadata service (k8s namespace: retention-compiler) and are pushed as policy bundles to the storage layer.
- TTL-config-snapshot.png is a UI export showing the policy bundle version and the effective TTL for the 'messages' and 'attachments' classes.
- For regulated customers we support a pinned configuration and can produce a signed timestamp when the policy was pushed.

If auditors need cryptographic attestations of the policy push, we can run an export and include the signed release artifact from our internal CI.
